00228.title: EMBRACE: eribulin Days 1 and 8 every 21 days
00228.population: 762 women with heavily pretreated locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer; 2-5 prior chemotherapy regimens, at least two for advanced disease, including anthracycline and taxane unless contraindicated.
00228.interpretation: Randomized phase III evidence supports this 21-day eribulin schedule in the studied advanced-breast population; median overall survival was 13.1 versus 10.6 months against physician's-choice treatment (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.66-0.99).
00228.limitations: Population-level historical trial results are not an individual prognosis, do not establish benefit in every line/subtype, and must not be copied to the 28-day schedule or liposarcoma. Trials report 1.4 mg/m² eribulin mesylate; the Irish/EU product dose is expressed as 1.23 mg/m² eribulin base. Never substitute the numeric dose expression without checking formulation.

separate_indication_evidence.title: Eribulin versus dacarbazine: advanced liposarcoma evidence
separate_indication_evidence.population: 452 adults with advanced liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after at least two systemic regimens including anthracycline, using Days 1 and 8 every 21 days.
separate_indication_evidence.interpretation: Separate sarcoma trial and its liposarcoma subgroup support the liposarcoma indication; breast-trial benefit figures do not apply.
separate_indication_evidence.limitations: The licensed liposarcoma indication must not be expanded to all sarcomas because the parent trial also enrolled leiomyosarcoma. Use current NCCP eligibility and EMA indication wording. Do not apply breast imaging or CA15-3/CEA pathways to liposarcoma.

00743.title: JUST-STUDY: eribulin Days 1 and 15 every 28 days
00743.population: Prospective multicentre phase II study: 88 patients with metastatic breast cancer previously exposed to anthracycline and taxane began standard eribulin; 42 changed to the biweekly schedule for tolerability and 40 continued standard treatment.
00743.interpretation: Provides schedule-specific feasibility and activity evidence for adaptation when the standard schedule is poorly tolerated.
00743.limitations: Schedule assignment was based on tolerability, not randomization. It does not prove equivalent efficacy or a phase III survival benefit for the 28-day schedule. Do not borrow EMBRACE survival numbers, extend to liposarcoma, or describe Days 1 and 15 as the EMA licensed schedule. The study's 1.4 mg/m² mesylate corresponds to the EU 1.23 mg/m² base expression.

00230.title: Gradishar phase III: nab-paclitaxel every 21 days
00230.population: 454 patients with metastatic breast cancer randomized to nab-paclitaxel 260 mg/m² every three weeks or solvent-based paclitaxel 175 mg/m² every three weeks.
00230.interpretation: Demonstrated higher response and longer time to tumour progression for this nab-paclitaxel dose/schedule, with more grade 3 sensory neuropathy and less grade 4 neutropenia than the comparator.
00230.limitations: This is formulation- and schedule-specific evidence, not evidence for superiority over contemporary weekly paclitaxel or every alternative therapy. Do not transfer to 100 mg/m² weekly, early breast cancer, other cancers or individual prognosis. NCCP's response review after two cycles takes precedence over a generic later imaging window.

00736.title: Weekly nab-paclitaxel: phase II schedule-specific evidence
00736.population: Patients with metastatic breast cancer progressing after conventional taxanes; 106 received 100 mg/m² and 75 received 125 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days.
00736.interpretation: Supports activity and tolerability of the weekly 100 mg/m² schedule. Separate randomized phase II first-line evidence included 100 and 150 mg/m² weekly schedules (Gradishar 2009).
00736.limitations: Neither trial specifically proves outcomes in a population selected for standard-paclitaxel hypersensitivity. The significant PFS comparison reported for 150 mg/m² in Gradishar 2009 must not be assigned to NCCP 100 mg/m². The weekly schedule is outside the licensed Irish indication described in NCCP 00736 and needs the specified consent/local approval pathway. Do not copy the q21-day phase III efficacy numbers.

00205.title: O'Brien phase III: PLD versus conventional doxorubicin in metastatic breast cancer
00205.population: 509 women with metastatic breast cancer and normal cardiac function receiving first-line chemotherapy; PLD 50 mg/m² every four weeks versus conventional doxorubicin 60 mg/m² every three weeks.
00205.interpretation: Comparable progression-free survival with less cardiotoxicity for PLD, while hand-foot syndrome and oral toxicity were more frequent. Overall survival was similar.
00205.limitations: Breast-trial findings do not establish efficacy in every NCCP 00205 cross-cancer indication. Normal cardiac function was required in this trial; lower cardiotoxicity does not mean cardiac safety in established heart disease or removal of monitoring. Do not interchange pegylated liposomal, non-pegylated liposomal and conventional doxorubicin.

advanced_breast_imaging.clinician_copy: For metastatic breast cancer, record baseline imaging and an individualized response-assessment plan. ESMO 2026 allows response evaluation approximately every 2-4 months, adjusted to symptoms, disease behaviour, disease sites and treatment. New or worsening symptoms prompt earlier assessment; this interval is not an automatic CT-TAP order for every patient.
advanced_breast_imaging.patient_copy: Your team will compare scans with your starting scans to see how treatment is working. The timing depends on your cancer and treatment, often every 2-4 months. Tell the team about new symptoms promptly; do not wait for the planned scan.
advanced_breast_imaging.cycle_mapping: After a documented clinician-selected interval, show cycle-relative milestones only as approximate examples. Three 21-day cycles are about 9 weeks; two or three 28-day cycles are about 8 or 12 weeks. Delays change the calendar. No dates or clinical inputs need to be entered to view the educational map.
advanced_breast_imaging.00230_override: Show an explicit response review after two 21-day cycles (about 6 weeks) under NCCP 00230. The team determines the scans/tests for that review; do not defer it to a generic 2-4-month milestone.
advanced_breast_imaging.boundary: This breast guidance is not automatically applied to liposarcoma or other PLD cancer indications. Brain imaging is symptom-, subtype- and management-dependent; avoid blanket claims that it is either universally routine or never indicated in asymptomatic patients.

tumour_markers.copy: CA15-3 or CEA may help follow selected metastatic breast cancers, particularly when initially elevated or disease is difficult to measure. Interpret trends with symptoms and imaging; marker change alone must not trigger treatment change. These tests are not mandatory for every patient or every cycle.
tumour_markers.boundary: This is a verified specific ABC5 statement, not a claim that all ABC8 text was reviewed. Do not equate tumour markers with cardiac troponin/BNP, or apply breast-marker monitoring to other cancers.

baseline_cardiovascular.copy: ESC recommends baseline clinical cardiovascular assessment and ECG for patients with cancer; additional cardiac imaging and biomarkers depend on treatment and cardiovascular risk. Distinguish this general baseline assessment from medicine-specific indications for serial ECG or echo.
baseline_cardiovascular.boundary: No routine HER2 every-three-month echo cadence is assigned to these cytotoxic monotherapies.

eribulin.copy: Review ECG/QT risk and medicines before starting. ECG monitoring is specifically recommended with heart failure, bradyarrhythmias, QT-prolonging medicines or electrolyte abnormalities. Correct low potassium, calcium or magnesium before treatment and monitor electrolytes periodically. Avoid eribulin in congenital long-QT syndrome. Assess peripheral neuropathy and blood counts with treatment reviews.
eribulin.boundary: The label reports a Day-8 QT observation from a small study; it does not mandate a universal Day-8 ECG schedule. Do not invent an ECG at every dose for every patient.

nab_paclitaxel.copy: Assess neuropathy and marrow/liver tolerance. Cardiac evaluation and repeat echo are driven by symptoms, prior cardiotoxic exposure and cardiac history, with NCCP-specific requirements retained. Remain alert to cardiac events and new respiratory symptoms.
nab_paclitaxel.boundary: No fixed three-month echo requirement is specified for nab-paclitaxel monotherapy. The formulation is not interchangeable with solvent-based paclitaxel; routine solvent-taxane premedication is not automatically copied.

pegylated_liposomal_doxorubicin.copy: Before starting, document cardiac history, prior anthracyclines and cardiac radiation, ECG, and LVEF by echo/MUGA. Repeat cardiac assessment periodically under the agreed risk-based plan. The Caelyx label recommends frequent ECG monitoring and mandates LV-function evaluation before each further administration that takes lifetime cumulative anthracycline exposure above 450 mg/m². New cardiac symptoms require prompt assessment.
pegylated_liposomal_doxorubicin.boundary: 450 mg/m² is a monitoring trigger, not a universally safe exposure ceiling or an automatic treatment-stop rule. Prior/concurrent cardiotoxic treatment matters, and toxicity can occur below this level. Any cumulative equivalent-dose calculation requires clinical/pharmacy verification. ESC anthracycline schedules are risk-stratified; do not silently turn them into a universal PLD echo cadence.

bone_density.copy: Do not add routine DEXA solely because one of these cytotoxic monotherapies is prescribed. If an accompanying endocrine, ovarian-suppression or bone-health plan requires DEXA, show that as a separate indication-specific milestone.
bone_density.basis: Implementation boundary: none of the three current product labels reviewed prescribes a universal DEXA schedule for these monotherapies.

supportive_care.verified_row: Table 1, PDF page 4: low emetogenic risk uses ondansetron 8 mg orally once on the treatment day; subsequent metoclopramide 10 mg orally up to three times daily as needed. The row does not state a rescue duration.
supportive_care.implementation: Retain a prescriber-confirmed duration and contraindication/renal/interactions review. Current NCCP guidance permits locally agreed alternatives and individual prescriber changes. Review eribulin/QT factors before selecting ondansetron or any alternative; no blanket substitution is inferred.
supportive_care.steroid_boundary: Antiemetic prophylaxis and infusion-reaction premedication are different purposes. Do not add solvent-paclitaxel steroid/antihistamine regimens automatically to nab-paclitaxel or PLD.

currency_and_access_limits: ABC8 was found as a September 2026 primary consensus publication (DOI 10.1016/j.breast.2026.104921; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960977626002316), but its full recommendations were not retrievable. It is not used to support a specific monitoring claim here.

Current ESMO 2026 publisher indexing directly supports the stated 2-4-month response interval. Detailed baseline imaging implementation is additionally grounded in the opened ESMO official pocket PDF; any new detailed 2026 recommendation not retrieved is not inferred.
All studies and product labels concern populations/regimens; they do not predict individual benefit. No claim of independent clinical or pharmacy sign-off is made.
